files.description: File paths to stage, relative to the repository root.

path.description: Repository path to run `git add` in.

cursor.description: Optional logs cursor to replay before switching to live websocket output.

branches.description: Short branch names present in the repository.

BranchRequest.description: Create or delete one named branch.

name.description: Branch name to create or delete.

paths.description: Paths to stream back as multipart file or error parts.

atomic.description: Replace each destination file atomically; fail that file if atomic replacement is unsupported.

CheckoutRequest.description: Switch the worktree to another branch.

CloneRequest.description: Clone a repository into a target directory.

branch.description: Branch to clone when `commit_id` is omitted.

commit_id.description: Commit to detach to after cloning.

depth.description: Optional shallow-clone depth. `1` clones only the tip commit.

insecureSkipTls.description: Skip TLS certificate verification for this clone invocation only.

password.description: Password for authenticated remotes; write-only and never returned.

url.description: Repository URL or local source path to clone.

username.description: Username for authenticated remotes; write-only and never returned.

allow_empty.description: Whether an empty commit is allowed.

author.description: Commit author name passed to git for this invocation only.

email.description: Commit author email passed to git for this invocation only.

hash.description: Full commit SHA of the created commit.

CompletionContext.description: Extra context for a completion request.

triggerCharacter.description: Trigger character when the completion was opened by one; omitted otherwise.

CompletionDocumentation.description: Completion documentation as plain text or structured markup.

detail.description: Short detail string shown beside the label; omitted when absent.

filterText.description: Filter key from the language server; omitted when absent.

insertText.description: Text inserted on accept; omitted when absent.

kind.description: LSP completion item kind enum value; omitted when the server left it unset.

sortText.description: Sort key from the language server; omitted when absent.

isIncomplete.description: Whether the server considers the list incomplete and expects re-querying.

items.description: Completion items, with non-contract keys pruned.

oneOf.description: Additional completion trigger context; omitted when none was provided.

pathToProject.description: Absolute project root path used as the server's workspace root.

position.description: Cursor position for which completions are requested.

limit.description: Maximum number of matches. Omitted or `<=0` uses the platform default.

role.description: Exact role filter. Omitted = any role.

scope.description: Scope selector: omitted or `focused` for the focused window, `pid` for one process, or `all` for all windows.

truncated.description: Whether traversal stopped because of node or wall-clock limits.

action.description: Optional action name for invoke requests.

id.description: The stable node id returned by tree/find.

value.description: Optional text value for editable nodes.

maxDepth.description: Maximum tree depth. Omitted or `-1` means unbounded.

scope.description: Scope selector: omitted or `focused` for the focused window, `pid` for one process, or `all` for all windows.

truncated.description: Whether traversal stopped because of node or wall-clock limits.

actions.description: Supported action names when the platform exposes them.

children.description: Child nodes when the response includes them.

id.description: Stable node id used by follow-up node actions.

value.description:
Current value of a control (a text field's contents, a checkbox's
state), when the platform reports it. Never set for secure (password)
fields. Capped by the platform; see `valueTruncated`.

valueTruncated.description: `value` was cut at the platform's cap.

ComputerUseActivityStatus.description: Activity status: `active` when the desktop is ready, otherwise `inactive`.

ComputerUseDesktopFailure.description: The failure attached to a `failed` desktop state.

code.description: The stable failure code callers branch on.

ComputerUseDesktopFailureCode.description: The reason the desktop entered the failed state.

id.description: Stable display index within the current desktop.

isActive.description: Whether this display is the active/focused display.

x.description: Display origin X coordinate in desktop pixels.

y.description: Display origin Y coordinate in desktop pixels.

modifiers.description: Modifier key names held while pressing `key`.

delay.description: Delay in milliseconds between key presses. Omitted = `0`.

ComputerUseLifecycleResponse.description: The response returned when starting or stopping the desktop.

double.description: Whether to double-click instead of single-clicking.

x.description: Target X coordinate in desktop pixels.

y.description: Target Y coordinate in desktop pixels.

endX.description: Drag end X coordinate in desktop pixels.

endY.description: Drag end Y coordinate in desktop pixels.

startX.description: Drag start X coordinate in desktop pixels.

startY.description: Drag start Y coordinate in desktop pixels.

x.description: Target X coordinate in desktop pixels.

y.description: Target Y coordinate in desktop pixels.

x.description: Target X coordinate in desktop pixels.

y.description: Target Y coordinate in desktop pixels.

ComputerUseProcessErrorsResponse.description: The stderr/errors of one named process.

ComputerUseProcessLogsResponse.description: The logs of one named process.

ComputerUseProcessRunningStatus.description: The running state of one named process.

running.description: Whether the named process is currently alive.

AutoRestart.description: Whether the process restarts automatically after exiting.

Failed.description: Whether the process entered a terminal failed state.

Pid.description: The live process id when `running` is true.

Priority.description: Relative startup priority among desktop processes.

RestartAttempts.description: Restart attempts used since the desktop was last started.

RestartBackoffMs.description: The current restart backoff in milliseconds.

Running.description: Whether the process is currently alive.

ComputerUseProcessStatusMap.description: The process-status map keyed by process name.

endTime.description: Recording end time in RFC 3339 format, omitted while live.

filePath.description: Absolute recording path inside the sandbox.

sizeBytes.description: Encoded file size in bytes when known.

startTime.description: Recording start time in RFC 3339 format.

label.description: Optional label used as the filename prefix.

desktop.description: The explicit desktop state after the restart succeeds.

status.description: Activity status; `active` after a successful restart.

format.description: Image format for compressed screenshot routes. Omitted = `png`.

height.description: Region height for region routes. Must be greater than zero.

quality.description: JPEG quality for compressed screenshot routes. Omitted = `85`.

scale.description: Downscale factor for compressed screenshot routes. Omitted = `1.0`.

show_cursor.description: Whether to include the current cursor position in the JSON response.

width.description: Region width for region routes. Must be greater than zero.

x.description: Region left coordinate for region routes.

y.description: Region top coordinate for region routes.

oneOf.description: Present when the caller asked for the cursor location.

sizeBytes.description: Size of the encoded image in bytes.

id.description: Desktop window identifier. Returned as an integer that JavaScript clients can represent exactly.

x.description: Window origin X coordinate in desktop pixels.

y.description: Window origin Y coordinate in desktop pixels.

CreateProcessQuery.description: Query parameters that change the call shape of `POST /processes`.

logs.description: Inline the first logs page using `text` or `base64`; requires `waitMs`.

waitMs.description: Wait up to this many milliseconds before replying; timing out still returns 201 with a running record.

argv.description: argv mode. Exactly one of `argv`, `shellCommand`, or `code` may be present.

code.description: Code to execute in an interpreter session.

cwd.description: Optional working directory. For `exec` and `pty`, defaults to the configured user’s home when available. Code execution, an explicit `user`, or an unavailable home uses the sandbox’s default working directory.

env.description: Environment overrides applied at spawn time.

oneOf.description: Process kind. Defaults to `exec`, or `code` when `code` is present. `session` starts a shell session and takes none of `argv`, `shellCommand` or `code`.

login.description: Whether to request a login shell.

name.description: Optional live-only alias. Must be a safe identifier.

sessionId.description: The session to run in. For `kind=exec`: the id or live name of a `kind=session` process; the `shellCommand` runs inside its shell, one command at a time, in order, and the request refuses `argv`, `cwd`, `env`, `shell`, `login: true`, `user` and `tag` (the session's settings apply; the command takes the session's tag). Unknown ids answer `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` (sessions are never created on first use) and an ended or deleted session answers `SESSION_ENDED`. For `kind=code`: the interpreter context to execute in.

shell.description: Requested shell path or shell name. For `kind=session` on Linux and macOS it must be a POSIX shell (bash, sh, dash, zsh, ksh): the session answers 400 `PROCESS_START_FAILED` when the shell does not run POSIX commands within 5 s of starting.

oneOf.description: Whether stdin stays open after create.

tag.description: Optional tag, a safe identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, 1-128 characters) that groups this process with others for `GET /processes?tag=` and `POST /processes:kill`. Applies to `kind=exec`, `pty` and `session`. `kind=code` refuses it, and so does a command run in a session, which takes the session's tag.

timeoutMs.description: Per-process timeout in milliseconds. For a session command, the timeout starts when execution begins, excluding time queued behind earlier commands. On expiry the command is stopped if possible. If it has not stopped after a further 5 seconds, the session and its background processes are ended.

user.description: Optional execution user. Not supported for `kind=code`; returns 400 `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION`.

cwd.description: Initial working directory. Empty uses the sandbox’s default working directory.

env.description: Environment overrides applied when the interpreter session starts.

id.description: Optional client-chosen session id. Must be a safe identifier when present.

kernel.description: Interpreter language, one of `python`, `typescript` or `javascript`. A language is required: `shell`, or omitting the field, answers 400 `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION`, because shell sessions are created with `POST /processes` `kind=session`.

login.description: Not supported for interpreter sessions; answers 400 `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` when `true`.

shell.description: Not supported for interpreter sessions; answers 400 `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` when set.

recursive.description: Recursive delete flag as a string query value.

DockerOwner.description: Who starts and owns Docker Engine in this sandbox.

DockerState.description: Where Docker Engine is in this boot's startup.

DockerStatus.description:
`GET /docker/status` — the Docker Engine startup status for this boot.
Read-only: asking never starts or restarts anything.

processId.description: ID of the process whose logs contain Docker output; read with `GET /processes/{id}/logs`. Null when no Docker process is available.

reason.description:
Why the state is what it is (a failure cause, a storage limitation,
or a note on a `ready` engine the sandbox user cannot reach). `null`
when there is nothing to add.

waitMs.description:
Wait up to this many milliseconds for a `starting` state to settle
before answering. Clamped to 1000; omitted or `0` answers immediately.

DocumentRequest.description: Identifies one document within a language-server workspace.

pathToProject.description: Absolute project root path used as the server's workspace root.

EnvRequest.description: Update environment variables for processes, PTYs, and sessions created after this call.

env.description:
Environment variables to add or replace for processes, PTYs, and sessions
created after this call. Keys must not also appear in `unset`.

unset.description: Names of previously added environment variables to remove. Keys must not also appear in `env`.

ErrorCode.description: Branchable domain codes. Fixed HTTP status per code — see x-daytona-error-codes. Once published, a code is contract: it can be added to, never renamed.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Error response body for every documented 4xx/5xx response. `code` is always present; `trace_id` may be omitted.

code.description:
A code from `x-daytona-error-codes` (the `ErrorCode` enum) or from
`x-daytona-generic-codes`.

source.description: Error source. Open vocabulary. SDKs match domain codes for `DAYTONA_DAEMON`; other sources use generic codes, then HTTP status.

trace_id.description: Recording trace identifier, omitted when unavailable.

ExitResult.description: Terminal result returned by `GET /processes/{id}/wait` and SSE `state` events.

exitCode.description: Process exit code, when the platform has one.

signal.description: Signal name such as `SIGKILL`, omitted when none applies.

FileInfo.description: One filesystem entry returned by `/files` and `/files/info`.

group.description: Numeric group id rendered as a string.

isDir.description: Whether the entry is a directory.

modTime.description: Last modification time as a formatted string. Prefer `modifiedAt` for RFC 3339 formatting.

mode.description: File mode string, for example `-rw-r--r--` or `drwxr-xr-x`.

modifiedAt.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp for the last modification time.

owner.description: Numeric owner id rendered as a string.

path.description: Absolute path to the entry, using the sandbox's path syntax.

extra.description: Extra path metadata; for renames this carries the original path, otherwise an empty string.

name.description: File or directory path reported by git.

FsPathQuery.description: Query parameters for routes that address one path or directory listing.

depth.description: Recursive listing depth for `GET /files`; omitted for the flat default (`1`).

path.description: Target path. Omitted on `GET /files` to use the sandbox’s default working directory.

GitConfigQuery.description: Query for one git config key.

GitConfigResponse.description: Value of one git config key.

value.description: Config value, or `null` when the key is unset.

GitPathQuery.description: Query for routes that operate on one repository path.

url.description: Remote URL with any userinfo redacted before it is returned.

buildSha.description: Toolbox build identifier, or `unknown` when unavailable. May be omitted.

buildTime.description: Toolbox build time in RFC 3339 UTC, or `unknown` when unavailable. May be omitted.

userHomeDir.description: Home directory of the configured default user; omitted when that user cannot be resolved. Without a configured default user, the toolbox's own home directory.

version.description: Platform release version, for example `2.0.0-alpha.1`; `0.0.0-dev` when unavailable. Distinct from the toolbox build identifier returned by `GET /version`.

bare.description: Whether to create a bare repository.

initial_branch.description: Initial branch name for a new non-bare repository.

path.description: Destination path for the new repository.

IsPortInUseResponse.description: Whether one TCP port is currently in use.

isInUse.description: `true` when the port is in use.

KeepLogs.description: Retention policy for process information and output logs.

KernelKind.description: Interpreter language. `/sessions` creates interpreter contexts; shell sessions are `kind=session` processes on `/processes`.

tag.description: The tag whose processes to kill: a safe identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, 1-128 characters).

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for every killed process to exit, in milliseconds. 1-60000; default 10000.

processIds.description: The tagged processes that were still running when the call started, and exited tagged processes that still had descendants running. Every one of them, and everything it started, has exited. Processes whose records were deleted or expired are killed too but not listed, so an empty list does not mean nothing was stopped.

Kind.description: What kind of process the API should run.

sessionId.description: Filter by the session a process ran in (`kind=session` process id or interpreter context id).

LogFrameDto.description: One log frame in a JSON log page or SSE `log` event.

data.description: Frame payload in the requested encoding.

cursor.description: Resume after this cursor. Empty or omitted starts from the beginning.

follow.description: When true, answer an SSE follow stream instead of a JSON page.

limit.description: Page size for JSON reads; clamped by the API.

MarkupContent.description: Rich-text documentation attached to a completion item.

file.description: Absolute path of the file containing the match.

Metrics.description: One snapshot of sandbox resource usage.

cpuCount.description: Logical CPU count visible inside the sandbox.

cpuUtilization.description: Fraction of total CPU capacity in use across all CPUs, between 0 and 1 inclusive.

diskTotalBytes.description: Total bytes on the filesystem containing the sandbox work directory.

diskUsageBytes.description: Used bytes on the filesystem containing the sandbox work directory.

memoryUsageBytes.description: Bytes of sandbox memory currently in use (`total - available`).

timestamp.description: Snapshot time as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

mode.description: Optional octal mode string; omitted or empty uses the route default.

group.description: Optional group id or name, when the platform supports chgrp.

owner.description: Optional owner id or name, when the platform supports chown.

path.description: Path whose permissions should change. On Linux, ownership and permissions apply to the symlink target when the path names a symlink.

PortList.description: The TCP ports currently listening inside the sandbox.

ports.description: All listening TCP ports inside the sandbox.

firstAvailableCursor.description: Cursor of the first surviving log frame, omitted when nothing was evicted.

lastCursor.description: Cursor of the last known log frame, omitted until at least one frame exists.

oneOf.description: Inline first logs page on `POST /processes?waitMs=...&logs=...`, omitted otherwise.

truncatedHead.description: Whether retention removed earlier output logs.

ProcessDto.description: Process information returned by create, get, and list operations.

cursor.description: Cursor at which the stream failed.

eof.description: Whether the process is terminal and there are no more frames after this page.

firstAvailableCursor.description: Cursor of the first surviving frame, omitted when nothing was evicted.

nextCursor.description: Cursor the client should pass to continue from the end of this page.

truncatedHead.description: Whether retention evicted older frames before this page.

argv.description: argv create shape, omitted unless this process was created that way.

code.description: Code source, omitted unless this is a `kind=code` process.

cwd.description: Working directory the API used. For a `kind=session` process, the session shell's current directory, updated after each command; for a command run in a session, the shell's directory when the command started.

exitedAt.description: RFC 3339 exit timestamp, omitted until terminal.

language.description: Code language, omitted when not applicable.

login.description: Whether the API requested a login shell.

name.description: Optional live-only alias, omitted when unnamed.

pid.description: OS process id while running, omitted before spawn and after exit. Always omitted for commands run in a session: they run inside the session's shell, whose own record carries its pid.

resolvedShell.description: Resolved shell path or name, omitted until resolution has happened.

sessionId.description: The session this process ran in: a `kind=session` process for shell commands, or the interpreter context for `kind=code`. Omitted for standalone processes.

shell.description: Requested shell, omitted when the API used its default resolution.

shellCommand.description: Shell command source, omitted unless this process was created that way.

signal.description: Signal name, omitted when none applies.

startedAt.description: RFC 3339 process-start timestamp, omitted until the process starts.

system.description: Whether this is a protected system process.

tag.description: The tag the process was created with, omitted when it has none. A command run in a session carries the session's tag. Never changes.

oneOf.description: PTY geometry, omitted for non-PTY processes.

timeoutMs.description: Process timeout in milliseconds, omitted when unset.

user.description: Requested user, omitted when the API runs as its default user.

cursor.description: Cursor of the stream position at which this state was emitted.

firstAvailableCursor.description: Cursor of the first surviving frame the client should resume from.

requestId.description:
Caller-generated identity, retained across retries (1–128 ASCII letters,
digits, underscores or hyphens). Replay is scoped to the active session.

waitMs.description:
Maximum HTTP wait in milliseconds. Expiry does not cancel accepted work.
Omitted means 30000. Zero submits a new request or retrieves a known one
without retrying it; only a wait above zero retries a retryable result.

manifestId.description: Version of remote volume data applied by a successful pull or observed when unchanged; null when unavailable or pending. An unchanged remote version does not guarantee that local files are unchanged.

requestId.description: The caller's stable request identity, including on elapsed waits.

newValue.description: Replacement text. Omitted only when the caller wants the route to reject the request.

error.description: Per-file error text, omitted on success.

file.description: Absolute or caller-supplied file path for this replacement attempt.

success.description: Whether the replacement succeeded for this file.

RepoRequest.description: Operate on a repository, optionally with credentials for a remote.

branch.description: Remote branch to push or pull. Omitted keeps the current HEAD push behaviour and git's default pull target.

password.description: Password for authenticated remotes; write-only and never returned.

remote.description:
Remote name. Omitted defaults to `origin` for push and for pull when
`branch` is set; a pull without `branch` uses git's configured upstream.

username.description: Username for authenticated remotes; write-only and never returned.

files.description: Optional pathspecs to reset in mixed mode.

mode.description: Reset mode (`mixed`, `soft`, `hard`, `merge`, `keep`); omitted means git's default mixed reset.

cols.description: PTY columns; must be at least 1.

rows.description: PTY rows; must be at least 1.

RestoreRequest.description: Restore paths from the index or another source.

source.description: Optional source tree-ish for the restore.

staged.description: Whether to restore the index entry.

worktree.description: Whether to restore the worktree entry.

pattern.description: Filename glob (`search`) or literal substring (`find`) pattern.

ServerRequest.description: Identifies a language-server instance for one language and one project root.

pathToProject.description: Absolute project root path used as the server's workspace root.

SessionDto.description: Session information returned by create, list, and get operations.

active.description: Whether the interpreter session is active.

cwd.description: Initial working directory of the interpreter session; changes made by executed code are not reflected here.

kernelProcessId.description: Process ID for the session's interpreter.

processIds.description: Member process ids in creation order.

escalateAfterMs.description: Grace period in milliseconds before escalating. Maximum 600000.

escalateTo.description: Escalation signal name. Defaults to `SIGKILL` when omitted.

signal.description: Signal name such as `SIGTERM`, `SIGKILL`, or `SIGINT`. Empty means `SIGTERM`.

State.description: Process lifecycle state: `starting`, optionally `provisioning`, then `running` and `terminal`. `provisioning` indicates that the execution environment is being prepared. See `ExitResult` for exit code, signal, timeout, or loss.

ahead.description: Commits the local branch is ahead of its upstream.

behind.description: Commits the local branch is behind its upstream.

branchPublished.description: Whether the current branch has an upstream.

currentBranch.description: Current branch name, or `HEAD` for a detached checkout.

StdinMode.description: Whether the process accepts live stdin writes.

data.description: Data to write. Text by default, or base64url when `encoding=base64`.

eof.description: Whether this request also closes stdin after writing.

location.description: Symbol location. Hierarchical symbols without an LSP `location` are normalized to an empty URI and zero range.

SymbolLocation.description: Location of a symbol in a document.

SymbolPosition.description: Zero-based line/character location within a document.

character.description: Zero-based UTF-16 character offset on the line.

SymbolsQuery.description: Query parameters shared by the symbol routes.

languageId.description: The LSP language key (`python`, `typescript`); required by both symbol routes.

pathToProject.description: Absolute project root path used as the server's workspace root; required by both symbol routes.

query.description: Workspace-symbol search string; required on `/lsp/workspacesymbols`, omitted on `/lsp/document-symbols`.

cols.description: Number of columns; must be at least 1.

rows.description: Number of rows; must be at least 1.

atomic.description: Replace the destination file atomically; fail if atomic replacement is unsupported.

path.description: Destination path for the uploaded file.

timeoutMs.description: Long-poll timeout in milliseconds. Omitted means the API's default 60-second chunk; `0` means wait until terminal; any positive value is honored uncapped.

isDir.description: Whether the changed entry is a directory.

name.description: Path relative to the watched root.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when the API emitted the event.

dropped.description: Whether the API dropped at least one watch event before it could emit it.

recursive.description: Whether nested subdirectories should be watched too.

info.description: The sandbox toolbox API: processes, sessions, files, Git, language servers, ports, metrics, volume pulls, and desktop automation. Every documented 4xx/5xx response uses `ErrorEnvelope`; codes and their HTTP statuses are listed in `x-daytona-error-codes` and `x-daytona-generic-codes`.

post.description: Send a signal, optionally with escalation, or interrupt a running code execution. On a Linux sandbox with process containment, `SIGTERM` and `SIGKILL` reach every process the target started, also after the target itself exited: such a request answers `PROCESS_TERMINAL` only once nothing it started is running.

parameters.description: Process id or live alias.
parameters.name: id

400.description: `BAD_REQUEST` or `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` — invalid signal request or an unsupported operation for this process kind.

403.description: `PROTECTED_PROCESS` — protected system processes cannot be signaled.

409.description: `PROCESS_TERMINAL` — the process has already exited (and, for `SIGTERM` or `SIGKILL` on a sandbox with process containment, nothing it started is still running).

422.description: `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` — the JSON body was well-formed but did not match `SignalRequest`.

500.description: Internal error while signaling the process.

422.description: `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` — the JSON body was well-formed but did not match `StdinRequest`.

get.description: Long-poll for the terminal result. Omitted `timeoutMs` keeps the API's default 60-second chunk, `timeoutMs=0` waits until terminal, and any positive value is honored uncapped. Timing out returns `reason: timed_out` without killing the process.

parameters.description: Long-poll timeout in milliseconds. Omitted means the API's default 60-second chunk; `0` means wait until terminal; any positive value is honored uncapped.
parameters.name: timeoutMs

post.description: Kill every process created with `tag`, and everything those processes started, including descendants that detached and the survivors of tagged processes that already exited. Returns only when none of them is running. Records and logs are kept. The tag can be used again right after the call.

200.description: Every process started under the tag has exited.

400.description: `BAD_REQUEST` — invalid tag or `timeoutMs`; `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` — this sandbox cannot contain processes (macOS, or a Linux guest whose kernel or cgroup mount lacks the support).

408.description: `PROCESS_KILL_INCOMPLETE` — some killed processes were still running when `timeoutMs` expired; call again to retry.

422.description: `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` — the JSON body was well-formed but did not match `KillProcessesRequest`.

post.description: Pull remote changes into an attached volume. Retain requestId across retries. Definitive results replay within the current session. A pending, unavailable or rate-limited result is retried only by a call with waitMs above zero; waitMs 0 returns the last outcome (a rate limit with its remaining delay) without retrying. An elapsed wait or disconnected caller does not cancel accepted work. A volume not attached to this sandbox returns a conflict. Replay is available only within the current session.

parameters.description: Attached volume ID (1–128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens).
parameters.name: volumeId

202.description: Pending; retry with the same requestId and waitMs above zero.

400.description: Invalid identifier/wait or malformed JSON.

409.description: The volume is not attached to this sandbox, requestId was reused for a different request, or the pull failed or was rejected.

413.description: Request body exceeds the JSON limit.

422.description: Invalid request shape, including unknown fields.

429.description: The pull request was rate-limited. The response includes requestId and retryAfterMs; Retry-After rounds up to one second.

503.description: Volume pull is temporarily unavailable; retain requestId for retry.
